pr.title: Add a project license to field.yaml, and --json to field explain and field arrangement (remote.md chunk 1)
pr.head: 2a1ef7617b8f544215e2543d5e25078e4628df39

summary: Field is a command-line tool that keeps a music project as plain files in Git and builds the project's audio from them. Its remote plan connects Field to audiofield.io, a site that hosts projects and plays their mixes. This pull request lands the plan's last chunk: two things the site reads from a project rather than from Field's build cache.

• A project license. field.yaml, the project's manifest, takes an optional license: holding an SPDX identifier such as CC-BY-4.0. SPDX is the standard list of short license names. Field checks only that the value looks like one, and the site decides which licenses a public project may use. field init --license writes it.
  • JSON from two read-only commands. field explain <label> describes one build target, and field arrangement <song> lists what a song places on its timeline. Each now takes --json and prints the value it already builds, under the TypeScript interface's field names, so a program can read it.

The plan held this chunk back until the site's render worker needed it. Justin chose on 2026-10-11 to land it now, since it needs no remote, and this pull request records that call in the plan's §9.1 and in docs/remote.md. The one open review finding is about how the plan was corrected: §8's definition of done and a §4 sentence were reworded in place, without the dated note this plan uses for every other correction.

cards.title: What the JSON carries
cards.html:
CommandPrintsNot in the JSON
explain --jsonExplanation: label, kind, rule, ruleVersion, inputs, parameters, actionKey, cached, fetched, outputs, file, choice, levelsNothing the text prints. An input not built yet has an empty sha256.
arrangement --jsonArrangementView: song, lengthTicks, and placements, each with track, at, bars, absolute, gainDb, and panEach placement's time in seconds, and the length in bars, which the text derives from the song's tempo and meter maps.

A key whose value is undefined, such as lengthTicks on a song with no length:, is left out rather than printed as null.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• SPDX identifier. A short standard license name, such as MIT or CC-BY-4.0. LicenseRef-… names a custom license.
  • Placement. An entry in a track's inputs: that puts another track on the timeline at a position, with a gain and a pan.
  • Tick. Field's unit of musical time. A song's tempo map turns ticks into seconds, and its meter map turns them into bar.beat.tick.
  • Explanation and ArrangementView. The typed values explain and arrangement build before printing, in src/graph/build.ts and src/commands/arrangement.ts.

cards.title: Overlap with #187
cards.html:
#187, open, adds muted to Placement and to Reach, the type behind explain's levels. These serializers print the interfaces whole, so once both land the JSON carries placements[].muted and levels.reaches[].muted with no further change. A cable whose sender placements are all muted shows as an empty arrivals list.

groups.title: The license in field.yaml
groups.kicker: An optional SPDX license in the project manifest, checked for shape and written by field init
intro: field.yaml is the project manifest: a format version, the project's name, and its sample rate. Its schema, projectSchema, is strict, so field check reports any key the schema does not list. This group adds license to the schema as an optional string that must look like an SPDX identifier.

The check is loose on purpose. Field accepts any SPDX-shaped string, including a custom LicenseRef-… one, and leaves the list of allowed licenses to the site. A fixed list would need a new Field release each time the site allowed another license (remote.md §5, decision 7). A missing license is not an error either, because whether a public project needs one is also the site's rule.

projectOrder lists the manifest's keys in the order field fmt writes them, and the license goes after name. field init --license <id> writes the key, and refuses a malformed one before it creates any file. Without the flag, init writes no license line.

checks.text: A project's license covers what the project's authors made. An imported sample keeps the license it arrived under. Whether field check should compare the two is left to the splice plan, which owns per-asset licenses (remote.md §9.10).

files.note: Adds SPDX_IDENTIFIER, the shape pattern, and the optional license key after name.

checks.text: Ran the pattern at this head against the licenses the site plans to accept (audiofield-io.md §10.5): CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, and CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 all pass, as do LicenseRef-mine and GPL-2.0+. CC BY 4.0, the empty string, and ids that start with - or . fail. The single-branch pattern accepts exactly what the earlier two-branch one did.
Ran field fmt on a field.yaml with license: before name. It moved the key after name, and field check had reported the file as not canonically formatted before that.

files.note: Refuses a malformed license before creating anything, then writes the license into the manifest.

checks.text: Ran field init --license 'CC BY 4.0' in an empty directory. It exits 1 with the SPDX message and leaves the directory empty.
Ran field init --license with 1.0, null, true, 0x1F, and 1e5, strings that YAML would read as other types. The emitter quotes each one, and field check passes on all five.

files.note: Pins the key order with and without a license, and the refusal in both init and check.

groups.title: JSON from explain and arrangement
groups.kicker: Two serializers that print the values the commands already build
intro: field explain <label> says what a build target is: its type, its inputs and their hashes, its cache key, whether its output is cached, and, for a track, where its signal goes and at what level. It builds that answer as an Explanation, then prints it as text. field arrangement <song> lists the tracks a song places on its timeline, in time order, as an ArrangementView, and formatArrangement turns that into text.

--json prints the same values with JSON.stringify. The field names are the interfaces' own, so a reader learns no second vocabulary, and a field added to either interface appears in the JSON with no further change (remote.md §5, decision 8). The serializers, explanationJson and arrangementJson, sit in the command modules, where tests can call them.

arrangement refuses a project with errors, because positions that never resolved would print as numbers that read like bar numbers. This group moves that refusal into validProject, so the text and JSON forms refuse the same projects.

checks.text: A placement's at and the song's lengthTicks are in ticks. The text form also prints each placement's time in seconds and the song's length in bars, which formatArrangement derives from the song's tempo and meter maps. The JSON carries neither, so a reader needs those maps from song.yaml, which is how the site already reads them (audiofield-io.md §13.9).
#187, open, adds muted to Placement and to Reach. Because these serializers print the interfaces whole, the JSON carries mute once both pull requests land.

Ran field explain //songs/tall-grass/track:room --json in examples/bloom. It carries the rule, the input, the parameters, the reach to main at −6 dB, and the drum-verb cable: everything the text form prints. Gains pass z.number(), which refuses infinity and NaN, so no gain prints as null.

files.note: arrangementJson, and the shared validProject check that both forms call.

checks.text: Ran field arrangement creek --json in examples/bloom. It prints song, lengthTicks: 46080, and the six placements the text form lists, in the same order. A valid project always has time:, so at is always in ticks.

files.note: The placements come back in time order, with their bars, gain, and pan.
An explanation round-trips through JSON to an equal object.

groups.kicker: --license on init, and --json on explain and arrangement
intro: src/cli.ts defines every field command with commander, a Node library for command-line options. This group adds the three flags and passes each to the code above. With --json, explain prints the JSON and returns before any text line.

files.note: Three new options, each passed to the code in the groups above.

groups.title: Docs and the plan
groups.kicker: The command manual, the project model, and the remote plan's record of the chunk
intro: docs/cli.md is the command manual, docs/project-model.md describes a project's files, and docs/remote.md describes how Field talks to the site. The remote plan, docs/projects/remote/readme.md, records each chunk as it lands in §10, keeps its open questions in §9, and states in §8 what has to be true before the plan is done. This group updates all four.

When a review proves this plan wrong, the plan keeps the old text and adds a dated *Amended (…):* paragraph, as in §3.3 and decisions 6 and 13. docs/projects/README.md asks for that. This pull request rewords §8 and a §4 sentence in place instead, which is the open review finding.

files.note: Describes the three flags, and says that an input not built yet has an empty sha256 in the JSON.
Lists the license and the sample rate in the manifest's one-line description.
Records the chunk in §10, adds a dated paragraph to §9.1, updates §9.8 and §9.10, and rewords §4 and §8.

checks.text: Read the plan at this head. §9.1 ends with this dated 2026-10-11 paragraph, and every other line that says chunk 1 is unstarted or waiting is an older dated paragraph with a newer dated entry after it.

§8's criteria "print the values their text forms show" and "fails field check with the file and line", and §4's claim that the site derives bar.beat from arrangement --json, are rewritten with no *Amended (…):* note saying what they replaced. A later check against §8 cannot tell that its bar moved in this pull request. Lines 311 and 603 also run to 115 and 87 columns in prose wrapped near 70. Add an amended note to §8 and §4 that quotes the earlier text, and rewrap the two lines.

files.note: The Pull section's closing paragraph now says the plan's chunks are complete and points at the CLI manual for the new flags. What remains is the definition of done: a real project cloned and built on a second machine.
